name: The Newbury Boston
insider_take: This Newbury Street icon isn't just a hotel—it's Boston's most prestigious address where literary legends once penned masterpieces and high society still gathers for afternoon tea.
whats_special: The Newbury sits on America's most expensive shopping street, occupying a prime corner where the Boston Public Garden meets Back Bay's Victorian brownstones. This historic property has hosted everyone from European royalty to Hollywood stars, maintaining its reputation as New England's most distinguished hotel since 1927.
pro_tip: Book a Public Garden view room—you'll overlook the same swan boats and tree-lined paths that inspired countless authors, plus enjoy front-row seats to Boston's stunning fall foliage display.
dont_miss: The hotel's legendary afternoon tea service in the Library Bar, where original manuscripts from famous guests are displayed. Step outside to explore the Freedom Trail starting just blocks away, or browse the luxury boutiques lining Newbury Street—Boston's answer to Rodeo Drive.
pros: Prime Back Bay location on Newbury Street for shopping and dining
Elegant luxury accommodations with sophisticated Boston charm
Exceptional personalized service and attention to detail
Historic property with modern amenities and refined atmosphere
cons: Urban setting with limited parking availability
